principles: Advisory-only: burn detection may never gate a lifecycle phase or produce gate evidence; desktop sessions are report-only (B-70e9 non-goal)
Reuse the existing pure-core scanners; zero writes to the transcript stores; no new daemon or config schema
Loud and actionable: a warning must name the concrete session file, cwd, and cumulative tokens so the operator can close that specific thread
Opt-in breakage only: plain doctor and plain usage_sweep keep their exit codes; only the explicit --alert mode exits non-zero
drivers: Advisory-only boundary is frozen at INIT: no gate wiring, gateEvidence=false, desktop sessions stay report-only
Reuse of the pure-core usage-sweep scanners with zero writes and bounded scan windows (doctor must stay fast)
Detection must not depend on operator memory: doctor habit covers interactive use, --alert non-zero exit covers cron

options.name: doctor advisory section + usage_sweep --alert (chosen)
pros: doctor is the habitual operator surface, so detection becomes push-based with zero new commands to remember
--alert non-zero exit composes with cron for unattended notification without lattice owning delivery
reuses core/usage-sweep.ts scanners verbatim; bounded recent-activity window keeps doctor fast
cons: detection still requires SOME lattice invocation (doctor habit or cron), not a true daemon
doctor gains a dependency on host transcript stores (mitigated by env kill-switch LATTICE_BURN_ALERT_RECENT_HOURS=0)

options.name: standalone watcher daemon (launchd/systemd) tailing transcript stores
pros: true real-time push; catches a runaway thread within minutes
cons: violates the CLI-first shape; needs install/lifecycle/permission management per host OS
a lattice-owned background process watching ~/.codex and ~/.claude is a much larger trust and review surface
overkill: burn accumulates over days, so a 48h-window doctor check catches it early enough

options.name: hook burn checks into every lattice command (preCommand hook)
pros: maximum coverage; any lattice usage surfaces the warning
cons: adds host-store scanning latency to EVERY command, including read-only ones
violates the read-only command contract (F-028 surfaces) and noise-floods normal workflows
alert fatigue: the same warning would print dozens of times a day

rationale: doctor is the habitual health surface so a burn section makes detection push-based with zero new commands; --alert composes with cron for unattended coverage; a daemon violates the CLI-first shape and a per-command hook would tax every read-only command. Empirical addendum: the 2026-07-12 B-8038 incident (0.92B real input in one day across 11 Codex Desktop threads, 98.4% cache reads, rollout files only 1-1.6MB) confirmed input-tokens is the load-bearing threshold and file-size is only a backstop.

preMortem.scenario: doctor becomes noticeably slow on machines with many huge recently-active transcripts
preMortem.trigger: several multi-hundred-MB rollouts with mtime inside the scan window force full stream-reads on every doctor run
preMortem.consequence: operators stop running doctor (alert fatigue defeats the push mechanism)
preMortem.mitigation: bounded default window (48h), stat-first cheap checks, documented LATTICE_BURN_ALERT_RECENT_HOURS=0 kill-switch; window and thresholds env-tunable without code changes

preMortem.scenario: existing doctor smokes become slow or nondeterministic
preMortem.trigger: doctor now scans the real ~/.codex and ~/.claude stores inside test processes
preMortem.consequence: unrelated smoke failures and flaky CI-like runs erode trust in the suite
preMortem.mitigation: existing doctor-invoking smokes set LATTICE_BURN_ALERT_RECENT_HOURS=0 around handler calls; the new burn-alert smoke covers the scan hermetically via injected fixture dirs

preMortem.scenario: --alert gets classified as a write and breaks read-only reviewer sessions or starts appending activity/process events
preMortem.trigger: ownership/activity classification keyed on the new flag by accident
preMortem.consequence: read-only contract regression (the exact F-014/F-028/F-032 class of bug B-70e9 fixed)
preMortem.mitigation: no changes to ownership-gate.ts/activity-policy.ts at all; smoke asserts {alert:true} resolves readOnly on both classification surfaces and plain-sweep dispatch stays byte-identical

preMortem.scenario: threshold env typos silently disable detection
preMortem.trigger: operator sets LATTICE_BURN_ALERT_INPUT_TOKENS=100M or an empty string
preMortem.consequence: burn scan silently runs with wrong/never-firing thresholds
preMortem.mitigation: resolver falls back to conservative defaults on any non-finite/negative value (never throws, never zeroes); smoke pins the fallback behavior per variable

preMortem.scenario: doctor async migration breaks a sync caller
preMortem.trigger: an unnoticed call site treats doctor() return as a string instead of a promise
preMortem.consequence: runtime type errors or [object Promise] output in a diagnostic surface
preMortem.mitigation: grep-enumerated call sites (registry dispatch already awaits; three smoke files updated to await); build is type-checked (tsc) so a missed site fails the build
